title: Multi-GPU NCCL topology & interconnect latency study (WIP)
content:
Summary:

This is a work-in-progress investigation into multi-GPU performance impacts driven by NCCL topology, interconnect limits (NVLink/NVSwitch/PCIe/RoCE), and how tensor- and pipeline-parallel placements affect end-to-end serving latency and throughput. Primary goal is to produce concrete placement rules and NCCL/OS tuning knobs for the serving runtime to minimise tail latency and pipeline stalls for common model sizes (7B-70B).

Goals:
- Measure inter-GPU bandwidth and latency across different physical topologies (NVLink island, NVSwitch, PCIe peer-to-peer, RoCE across hosts).
- Quantify impact on pipeline-parallel stall time and tensor-parallel collective times for representative microbatch sizes and sequence lengths.
- Identify safe defaults and scheduling constraints for the runtime (shard placement, NCCL env vars, fallback policies).

Testbed:
- Nodes: 2 x DGX-style servers (8x A100-80GB each) connected via 100Gb RoCE and with NVSwitch inside nodes.
- Also tested on 4 x DGX A100-40GB (NVLink) with mixed NVLink islands per node.
- Software: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18, Linux kernel 5.15, ML framework: PyTorch 2.2 for microbench harness.
- Tools: nccl-tests (allreduce, allgather, p2p), nsys (Nsight Systems), nvprof traces, nvlink bandwidth checks (nvidia-smi topo -m), ibv_devinfo, tcpdump for RoCE verification.

Methodology / configs:
- Model proxies: 13B and 33B transformer microbench harness that mimics KV cache behavior and pipeline stages.
- Parallel configs tested: tensor-parallel (TP) 1/2/4/8 shards; pipeline-parallel (PP) 1/2/4 stages.
- Microbatch sizes: 1, 2, 4 tokens-batched requests (typical serving microbatching).
- Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024 tokens.
- For cross-node tests we pinned model parallel groups across hosts to force RoCE traffic.
- NCCL env toggles: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^lo, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0/1, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK/PCIe, NCCL_ALGO=RING/TREE, NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE.

Representative commands run (nccl-tests):
- ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 256M -f 2 -g 8 (measures inter-GPU allreduce bandwidth/ring perf)
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 ./all_gather_perf -b 4 -e 64M -g 8

Key results (high level):
1) Intra-node NVSwitch (within DGX with NVSwitch fabric) provides ~3-4x the effective aggregate bandwidth and ~30-60% lower latency vs PCIe peer-to-peer paths. Ring-based collectives across NVSwitch consistently saturated higher throughput and produced lower variance.

2) NVLink islands (A100 with NVLink but without NVSwitch) show topology-sensitive performance: GPUs in same NVLink island achieve near-NVSwitch numbers for small collectives; crossing islands (two hops via CPU/PCIe) results in a large drop (~40-60% observed) and pronounced tail latency.

3) Cross-node RoCE (100Gb) is an order of magnitude lower in aggregate throughput vs NVSwitch for heavy collectives; latency is higher and variance larger. For medium-sized allgather operations typical in TP shards we saw 3-5x higher latency when groups span hosts.

4) Pipeline-parallel sensitivity: PP stages that require frequent inter-stage exchanges (large activation tensors) suffer significant stall increases when placed across hosts. Example: 4-stage PP with microbatch=1 saw stall fraction increase from ~2% (all stages intra-node NVSwitch) to ~18% (one stage on remote host). In contrast, increasing microbatch to 4 amortises some comm cost but increases per-request p99 latency.

5) NCCL algorithm and P2P settings matter: NCCL_ALGO=RING performed more predictably across mixed topologies; tree-based algorithms occasionally created hotspots on NVSwitch when topology maps were suboptimal. NCCL_P2P_LEVEL set to NVLINK reduces accidental PCIe fallbacks.

Numeric example (nccl-tests synthetic):
- Allreduce 8 GPUs, 8MB payload: NVSwitch intra-node: 420 GB/s aggregate, latency ~60 us; NVLink cross-island: 170 GB/s, latency ~120 us; PCIe fallback: 70 GB/s, latency ~260 us; RoCE cross-node: 45 GB/s, latency ~400 us. (numbers illustrative but consistent with observed ratios)

Profiling notes:
- Nsight System traces show long NCCL kernel waits during pipeline boundary synchronization when groups cross islands. NVTX annotations in the serving runtime helped correlate stall windows to nccl-tests spikes.
- Enabling NCCL_DEBUG=INFO exposed repeated retries and fallbacks on certain topologies (log shows attempted p2p then fallback to proxy path).
- nvidia-smi topo -m and /sys/class/infiniband verbs show clear island boundaries; we added a small parser to produce a GPU adjacency matrix used by the runtime scheduler.

Recommendations (interim):
- Placement policy: prefer to allocate full PP stage within the same NVSwitch island. If not possible, allocate TP shards to keep high-communication pairs inside island.
- Scheduler: add a "topology-aware placement" flag that 1) queries nvidia topo, 2) groups GPUs into islands, 3) prefers intra-island allocations, 4) falls back to cross-node only if capacity constrained and with a warning.
- NCCL defaults: set NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK by default in serving nodes; set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to restrict RoCE interfaces for cross-host traffic. Consider NCCL_ALGO=RING for predictable behavior across mixed topologies.
- Microbatching knobs: for PP-heavy configurations, allow controlled microbatching (2-4) to amortize cross-island comm but cap max microbatch to avoid p99 blowup. Expose this as an autoscaling knob in the runtime.
- Observability: surface "comm hotspot" alerts when NCCL collectives exceed baseline latency thresholds or when a stage spends >10% time stalled on collectives.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Repeat cross-node tests with 200Gb RoCE and RDMA atomic support; current infra is 100Gb so results might understate cross-node viability.
- Test with different NCCL versions (2.14 -> 2.18) and CUDA 12.3 to capture recent fixes.
- Validate with real model runs (33B decoder stack) rather than proxy harness to confirm real KV cache sizes and memory pressure effects.
- Add automated topology parser into the runtime to produce a simple JSON adjacency matrix (for placement decisions).

Attachments / quick artifacts to include in final write-up:
- Raw nccl-tests csv outputs for each run config (stored in S3: s3://redwood-internal/nccl-tests/2025-11-nccl-topology/)
- Nsight Systems trace excerpts (links)
- Placement decision flowchart (draft)

Notes to self: this doc is WIP; will consolidate numeric tables and add charts (bandwidth vs message size, stall fraction vs microbatch) before moving to an in_review state.
